statement: The floor power of a base-2 repunit is closed form, and it is the first exact floor-power value in this laboratory off the perfect-power locus. LEMMA 8 IN BASE TWO. x = -1 mod 2^a says the low a bits of x are all 1, so run(x) = v_2(x+1) is the number of TRAILING ONE-BITS of x and the floor x >= 2^a - 1 is attained exactly when every bit is one, at the repunits M_a = 2^a - 1. The landing point is the base-3 repdigit: M_a = (1^a)_2 maps in exactly a shortcut steps to 3^a - 1 = (2^a)_3, and the continuation is lifting the exponent -- exactly v_2(3^a - 1) halvings, which is 1 for odd a and 2 + v_2(a) for even a -- so the word opens O^a E^1 or O^a E^(2+v_2(a)). Those three are elementary restatements of the congruence. THE CLOSED FORMS, WHICH ARE NOT. For even a >= 2, floor((2^a - 1)^(3/2)) = 2^(3a/2) - 3*2^(a/2 - 1), binary 1^(a-1) 0 1 0^(a/2 - 1), so the floor charge against the top of the cell 2^(3a/2) is exactly 3*2^(a/2 - 1). Proof: (1-x)^(3/2) = 1 - (3/2)x + (3/8)x^2 + ... at x = 2^(-a) gives 2^(3a/2) - 3*2^(a/2-1) + delta with delta = (3/8)2^(-a/2)(1+o(1)) in (0,1), and for even a both leading terms are integers. Verified to a = 400, bit pattern to a = 40, delta measured 0.1962, 0.0948, 0.0470, 0.0235 halving per step of 2 in a as the expansion predicts. For ODD a the leading term is irrational and the value is a Beatty value, floor((2^a-1)^(3/2)) = floor(sqrt 2 * K) with K = 2^((3a-1)/2) - 3*2^((a-3)/2), verified to a = 200 -- whose digits are binary digits of sqrt 2, the same 2-adic-to-Archimedean seam the exponent bridge found at the end of an exact even tower, here off the exact locus. THE FAMILY IS THE RIGHT CONTRAST. By Catalan, proved by Mihailescu (mihailescu-2004-catalan), 2^a - c^k = 1 has no solution with c,k >= 2, so M_a is never a perfect power for a >= 2 and exactRun(M_a) = 0: the repunits are maximally INEXACT starts, the opposite of the locus where floorPower_of_even_sq, floorPower_of_odd_sq and the pow_two_depth family live. So the floor charge is not intrinsically unknowable away from perfect powers, only unknowable generically. THE PRIMALITY IS DECORATIVE. The floor is attained at 2^a - 1 for every a, prime or not: 15 = 3*5, 63 = 7*9, 255, 511 = 7*73 all have run = a. What is structural is u = x + 1 = 2^a, the least value with v_2(u) >= a; 'Mersenne' is u - 1, an artifact of that coordinate, and under the exponential bridge of J-lemma-eight-is-the-exponent-valuation the extremal transports to the exponent e = 2^r -- one one-bit, not a repunit -- so the all-ones pattern does not survive the transport and carries no prime content in either problem. One family of density zero: no bound moves, no cycle is touched, N_0 is unchanged. THE WHOLE RUN, NOT ONLY ITS ENDS (added 20 September after reading the MathWorld entry). T(2^n - 1) = 3*2^(n-1) - 1, so inductively T^j(2^n - 1) = 3^j * 2^(n-j) - 1 for 0 <= j <= n, which at j = n is the repdigit. In binary that is (3^j - 1)2^(n-j) + (2^(n-j) - 1): the bits of 3^j - 1 followed by exactly n - j ones. So the trailing-one block shrinks by exactly one per step and its length is the number of steps REMAINING -- Lemma 8's countdown is visible in base two at every step of the run, not only at its two ends. Checked to n = 200 for the value and n = 40 for the bits; at n = 4 the run reads 1111, 10111, 100011, 110101, 1010000. WHAT THE STATEMENT DOES NOT NEED. MathWorld records that all known M_p with p prime are squarefree while Guy (1994) believes some are not, so squarefreeness of Mersenne numbers is OPEN. exactRun(M_a) = 0 does not need it: squarefree implies not a perfect power and the converse fails, so the property we use is strictly weaker, and it is a theorem. The squarefree route would also fail outright at composite indices -- M_6 = 63 = 3^2 * 7 is not squarefree yet still not a perfect power -- while Catalan covers every a >= 2. TWO FURTHER COINCIDENCES, BOTH KILLED. (i) The Mersenne numbers are a Fermat polynomial at x = 1 and satisfy F_n = 3F_(n-1) - 2F_(n-2), coefficients 3 and 2. NUMEROLOGY: the characteristic polynomial is (t-1)(t-2) = t^2 - 3t + 2 because 2^n - 1 combines 1^n and 2^n, so the 3 is the trace 1 + 2 and the 2 is the determinant, neither being the 3 of 3x + 1. (ii) The run ends at 3^n - 1, of binary length floor(n log2 3) + 1 = A020914(n), the laboratory's distinguished word length. RESTATEMENT: A020914(n) IS the binary length of 3^n, and the Mersenne word length n + v_2(3^n - 1) is unrelated to it (4 against 5 at n = 3, 6 against 8 at n = 5). ONE USEFUL FRAMING. M_n is the Cunningham number C^-(2,n), a one-base object; the cycle gap 3^o - 2^K is not, having two bases and two independently moving exponents, which is the precise and citable reason classical primitive-divisor theory (Zsigmondy, Bang, Carmichael) does not reach it. THE WITNESS HAS A NAME (added after checking the OEIS factorisation sequences the MathWorld entry cites; oeis.org is blocked by this environment's egress policy, so the quoted terms were re-derived rather than read -- A000225, A114475, A046051, A085724, A049479, A005420 all reproduce; A034887 looked like a mismatch and was recorded here as an offset error of mine with the sequence indexed from n = 1. THAT CORRECTION WAS ITSELF WRONG AND IS RETRACTED, 20 September, from a local mirror of the OEIS (github.com/oeis/oeisdata, export stamped 2026-09-20, reachable from this container although oeis.org is not): A034887 carries offset 0 and its 73 stored terms match the decimal digit counts of 2^n indexed from n = 0 exactly, while indexing from n = 1 does not match at all, so indexing from 0 -- what was done originally -- was right. What produced the original apparent mismatch is not reconstructible and is deliberately not replaced with a fresh guess; nothing in this row depends on it). The cyclotomic factorisation is 2^n - 1 = prod over d | n of Phi_d(2), and Phi_2(2) = 3 = Phi_6(2) = 2^2 - 2 + 1 is the unique collision, so M_6 = 1 * 3 * 7 * 3 = 63 = 3^2 * 7. That single coincidence simultaneously kills the primitive prime divisor at n = 6 -- Bang 1886, the base-2 case of Zsigmondy, whose only exceptions are n = 1 and n = 6, exhibited here through n = 14 -- AND creates the square. So the squarefreeness witness a = 6 above is the named exceptional index rather than an arbitrary composite. THE NEGATIVE USE IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. Bang and Zsigmondy govern a^n - b^n with ONE moving exponent; the cycle gap 3^o - 2^K moves two independently and is not a Cunningham number, which is the precise and citable reason classical primitive-divisor theory does not reach it. Registry entry zsigmondy-1892-primitive-divisors; neither Bang nor Zsigmondy nor Cunningham appeared anywhere in the repository before. THE BASE-TWO READING HAS PRIOR ART AND NOW CARRIES A CITATION (20 September, from the A000225 entry text). A comment by Michel Lagneau of 18 January 2012 on OEIS A000225 states that a(n) = 2^n - 1 is the number k for which the count of iterations of k -> (3k+1)/2 remaining odd, until the result is even, equals n -- which is exactly run(2^n - 1) = n, the Lemma 8 floor attained at the repunits, verified here for n <= 12 under both readings of the count. So the base-two reading was in the literature fourteen years before this row and is KNOWN (oeis-A000225), not merely an elementary restatement; the closed forms for the Juggler image remain the row's own content. The same entry confirms the Fermat-polynomial kill with the standard name -- A000225 is the Lucas U(P=3,Q=2) sequence, so the 3 and 2 are the trace and norm of the roots {1,2} -- and it supplies the sharpest form of the primality verdict: A000225 is 2^n - 1 for every n while A001348 restricts to n prime, and the floor is attained on A000225 with composite indices included, so the OEIS split between the two sequences IS the statement that the primality is decorative. Zsigmondy 1892 is itself a link on A000225, which is where the primitive-divisor framing should have been found from. REPUNIT TO REPUNIT, WHICH IS THE RIGHT FORM OF THE LANDING STATEMENT. The A000225 generalisation comment, a(n) = (A^n - 1)/(A-1) with A003462 the A = 3 case, names (3^a - 1)/2 as the base-3 repunit, and the landing point 3^a - 1 is exactly twice it. So one further halving lands on the repunit itself: T^(a+1)(2^a - 1) = (3^a - 1)/2 = A003462(a), checked to a = 200. Stated properly, the run takes a ONES IN BASE 2 to a ONES IN BASE 3 in exactly a + 1 steps -- A000225(a) to A003462(a) -- which is cleaner than the earlier 'all ones in base two to all twos in base three', and it is the end of the initial run exactly when a is odd, since v_2(3^a - 1) = 1 there and 2 + v_2(a) when a is even. PRIORITY CORRECTION, 20 SEPTEMBER: THE WHOLE-RUN CLOSED FORM IS WILLIAMS 2026. Her principal skeleton L_1 has elements 2^a 3^b - 1 at (a,b), her Section 5.1 names column b = 0 as the Mersenne numbers and b = 1 as the Thabit numbers, and traversing her row k = a from (a,0) by the diagonal flow gives exactly 2^(a-j) 3^j - 1 -- IDENTICAL to T^j(2^a - 1) = 3^j 2^(a-j) - 1, checked term by term to a = 120. Her Proposition 3.10 is the boundary continuation v_2(3n+1) = 1 + v_2(lambda 3^(b+1) - 1), which at lambda = 1 is the LTE statement recorded above. So the Collatz-side run description, the Mersenne column and the repunit-to-repunit landing are all hers and are NOT NEW; primes in L_1 are the Pierpont primes of the second kind, OEIS A005105, and the Thabit column is A055010. WHAT STANDS is the Juggler content, which her paper does not contain: floor((2^a - 1)^(3/2)) = 2^(3a/2) - 3 * 2^(a/2 - 1) for even a with bits 1^(a-1) 0 1 0^(a/2-1), the odd-a Beatty form floor(sqrt 2 * K), the fact that these are exact floor-power values OFF the perfect-power locus since 2^a - 1 is never a perfect power by Catalan, and the Bang/cyclotomic account of the a = 6 witness.
